IDQ20809
Australian Government Bureau of Meteorology

Minor Flood Warning for the Bremer River and Warrill Creek

Issued at 7:46 pm AEST on Tuesday 3 November 2026
Flood Warning Number: 2


MINOR FLOODING POSSIBLE ALONG BREMER RIVER AND WARRILL CREEK WITH STORMS FROM OVERNIGHT
TUESDAY INTO WEDNESDAY

Rainfall totals up to approximately 20 mm have been recorded across the Bremer and Warrill
catchments since late Tuesday afternoon. Further showers and thunderstorms are possible
during Tuesday evening and into early Wednesday. Heavy rain remains possible in parts of
the catchments with thunderstorm activity, though the timing and location of heavy falls
remain uncertain.

Catchments are relatively wet and are likely to respond quickly to rainfall. Depending on
the timing and location of the heaviest falls, minor flooding may develop along the Bremer
River and Warrill Creek from overnight Tuesday into Wednesday. Higher levels may be
possible. The situation is being closely monitored and this warning will be updated as
required.

Warrill Creek:
Minor flooding is possible with forecast thunderstorm activity along Warrill Creek.

No observations are currently available for the Warrill Creek at Kalbar. With forecast
rainfall, the Warrill Creek at Kalbar may exceed the minor flood level (6.00 m) overnight
Tuesday into Wednesday.

The Warrill Creek at Harrisville is currently at 0.80 m and steady, below the minor flood
level. With forecast rainfall, the Warrill Creek at Harrisville may exceed the minor flood
level (3.00 m) in the early hours of Wednesday.

The Warrill Creek at Amberley is currently at 1.44 m and steady, below the minor flood
level. With forecast rainfall, the Warrill Creek at Amberley may exceed the minor flood
level (4.00 m) Wednesday morning.

Bremer River:
Minor flooding is possible with forecast thunderstorm activity along the Bremer River.

The Bremer River at Rosewood is currently at 0.62 m and steady, below the minor flood
level. With forecast rainfall, the Bremer River at Rosewood may exceed the minor flood
level (4.00 m) in the early hours of Wednesday.

The Bremer River at Five Mile Bridge is currently at 0.10 m and steady, below the minor
flood level. With forecast rainfall, the Bremer River at Five Mile Bridge may exceed the
minor flood level (3.50 m) in the early hours of Wednesday.

The Bremer River at Walloon is currently at 1.64 m and steady, below the minor flood
level. With forecast rainfall, the Bremer River at Walloon may exceed the minor flood
level (5.00 m) early Wednesday morning.

Safety Advice:
* Don't drive, walk, swim or play in floodwater because it is dangerous.
* Stay away from flooded drains, rivers, streams and waterways.
* Obey road closure signs. Plan ahead so you don't drive on flooded roads.
* Check the ABC and local media for updates. The situation can change quickly, so stay
informed.
* For local emergency management warnings and advice visit
www.disaster.qld.gov.au/warnings.

For emergency assistance call SES on telephone number 132 500. In life-threatening
emergencies, call 000 (triple zero) immediately.

Next issue:
The next warning will be issued by 03:00 PM AEST on Wednesday 04 November 2026.
